# Downloads {#sec-downloads .unnumbered}

This page provides access to the latest version of the book and to the release of the dataset that its chapters use.
Versioned releases for major editions will be added as the project evolves.


## Latest Book Version

These files are automatically updated whenever the book is rebuilt.

- [Download PDF (latest)](/downloads/book-latest.pdf)
- [Download EPUB (latest)](/downloads/book-latest.epub)
- [Download DOCX (latest)](/downloads/book-latest.docx)


## Charles River Accounting Dataset

The Charles River Accounting Dataset supports every chapter of the book across Excel, SQL, and Power BI.
The files are hosted on GitHub Releases to support large file sizes and fast global downloads.
Visit the [Charles River Accounting Dataset website](https://charlesriver.accountinganalyticshub.com/)
for documentation and additional information. All dataset changes and updates
will be posted there.

This edition of the book is verified against dataset release {{< var dataset.version >}}, which covers {{< var dataset.window >}}.
Use the files below, which come from that release, so that your results match the chapters. A later release of the dataset can contain different values.

- [Charles River Accounting Dataset (SQLite)]({{< var dataset.download >}}/CharlesRiver.sqlite)
- [Charles River Accounting Dataset (Excel)]({{< var dataset.download >}}/CharlesRiver.xlsx)
- [Charles River Accounting Dataset (CSV package)]({{< var dataset.download >}}/CharlesRiver_csv.zip)

All three formats contain the same Charles River data, so students can move between Excel, SQL, and Power BI without changing datasets.
The [release page]({{< var dataset.release >}}) lists each file's SHA-256 checksum, which you can use to confirm a download.

## Supplementary Material {#sec-companion-files}

Each chapter's slides, companion files, and solutions are in the table below. **Slides** are the chapter's PowerPoint deck; the chapter page also lets you view them in the browser. **Companion files** are the start files of the tutorials: each holds the work as it stands at the end of the previous tutorial, and a chapter-end file closes the set, so you can begin a tutorial without the one before it or check your own work. **Solutions** cover the exercises, the comprehensive cases, and the capstone cases, so try the work first. Every file explains itself, in a **Solution Notes** worksheet, a Power BI **Notes** page with a **Checks** query, or a SQL script's header and notes block.

### Opening a Companion File

The Excel and Power BI files read CharlesRiver.xlsx from the folder `C:\CharlesRiver`. If your copy is there, a file is ready to refresh. Otherwise, point the file at your copy once, before you refresh it. The Power BI solutions of the capstone cases also read their case's solution workbook, and Chapter 19's reads RefundFlags.csv, from the same folder.

In Excel:

1. Select **Data > Get Data > Data Source Settings**.
2. Select the CharlesRiver.xlsx source and **Change Source**, browse to your copy, and select **OK**.
3. Close the dialog and select **Data > Refresh All**.

The Power BI files are Power BI projects: a .pbip file and two folders with the same name, which hold no data until you refresh them. In Power BI Desktop:

1. Copy the .pbip file and its two folders into a folder of your own, and open the .pbip file.
2. Select **Home > Transform data > Data source settings**, select the CharlesRiver.xlsx source and **Change Source**, browse to your copy, select **OK**, and close the dialog.
3. Select **Apply changes** if a bar offers it, or **Refresh** on the **Home** tab.
4. Select **File > Save as** and save a .pbix file with the name the tutorials use, such as Charles River Reports.pbix.

The new Power Query experience, a preview feature, has no **Change Source** button, so if you turned it on, turn it off in **File > Options and settings > Options > Preview features** first.

The SQL scripts need no change of source. Save a script in the folder of your working copy, CharlesRiver_Work.sqlite (Tutorial 9.1), open the copy in DB Browser for SQLite, and open the script from the **Execute SQL** tab with **Open SQL file(s)**. The Part III case uses the view that Tutorial 11.3 saves in the working copy. If you skipped that tutorial, run Setup_Part3_Views.sql once and select **Write Changes**.
